title: Sara Blakely: $5,000 in Savings to Billion-Dollar Spanx
description:
Sara Blakely started Spanx in 2000 with $5,000 in savings, after seven years selling fax machines door to door. Hosiery mills turned her down before one agreed to make her footless pantyhose; Oprah featured Spanx in November 2000. In 2012 Forbes named her the youngest self-made woman billionaire, at 41, while she still owned 100% of the company with no debt and no outside investors. In 2021 Blackstone bought a majority stake valuing Spanx at $1.2 billion; Blakely kept a significant stake (the price paid was not disclosed). Billionaire status depends on estimates: Fortune reports her net worth fell below $1 billion in 2020. The lesson: test a cheap fix for a problem you actually have before you spend big.

Sources: CNN Business (Oct 21, 2021); Reuters via CNBC (Oct 20, 2021); Forbes World's Billionaires 2012, as reported by CNN Business, The Week and Marketplace (Mar 14, 2012); CNBC (Apr 3, 2019); Fortune (Sept 20, 2025) for the fax-machine years, mill rejections, Oprah and first-year sales ($4M, then $10M; Spanx is private, so these are company/founder figures). Educational content, not investment advice.

Mills said no. Then one agreed.
Oh-pruh featured it in two thousand. Sales: four million, then ten million.
By twenty twelve, Forbes called her a billionaire.
Now the twist: she'd never taken a single outside investor.
In twenty twenty-one, Blackstone bought control, valuing Spanx at one point two billion.
The lesson: test a cheap fix for a problem you actually have.
